proposed_relationship: Combining mechanical cleavage of layered materials with the knowledge of hexagonal boron nitride's structure could lead to the creation of strictly two-dimensional boron nitride crystals.
mechanism: The mechanical cleavage technique can be applied to hexagonal boron nitride to thin it down to a single layer, effectively creating a two-dimensional crystal. This process exploits the weak van der Waals forces holding the layers together, allowing for the separation of individual layers. By doing so, it may be possible to create a material that, despite theoretical predictions of thermodynamic instability at finite temperatures, could exhibit unique properties due to its reduced dimensionality.
constraint_released: The constraint of three-dimensional stability is released, potentially allowing for the observation of novel physical phenomena in a strictly two-dimensional boron nitride crystal.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: 0.33 nanometers (theoretical thickness of a single layer of hexagonal boron nitride)
